name: Tessera Phantom Mark IV 'Ghost Writer'
description:
Tessera's flagship suppressed precision platform fires caseless subsonic rounds through a 14-baffle integral suppressor that reduces the weapon's acoustic signature to below 60 decibels. The Phantom Mark IV was designed for deniable operations in urban environments where gunfire would attract immediate response.

The rifle uses a delayed-blowback action tuned for absolute reliability with subsonic ammunition, and the barrel incorporates a thermal masking sleeve that dissipates heat signatures within seconds of firing. At effective range, the only indication of a Phantom shot is the impact itself.

Tessera markets the weapon exclusively through classified procurement channels, and each unit is serialized with a quantum-dot identifier that the company claims is impossible to remove. Street armorers disagree, and a thriving black market exists for 'cleaned' Phantoms with their identifiers acid-etched away.
legality: Classified procurement only — corporate or state actors
specifications: caliber: 8.6mm caseless subsonic effective_range: 50-800 meters rate_of_fire: Semi-automatic, 1 round per second capacity: 10-round detachable magazine weight: 5.4 kg power_source: None — conventional mechanical action
tactical_use: The Ghost Writer excels in urban assassination where stealth outweighs raw stopping power. Operators pair the weapon with BCI-linked optics that compensate for the subsonic round's pronounced bullet drop at range. The weapon is favored for operations inside GLMZ's enclosed arcology levels where sound carries unpredictably and a single unsuppressed shot can trigger automated security responses across multiple sectors.
cultural_context: The phrase 'ghost writing' has entered GLMZ slang to describe any covert action carried out with professional precision. When someone dies without witnesses, without sound, and without forensic evidence, people say they were 'ghost written.' Tessera neither confirms nor denies the weapon's existence in public channels.
story_hooks: Three mid-level corporate managers from competing firms were ghost written in the same week — all killed with 8.6mm caseless rounds. Someone is pruning a corporate org chart.
A cleaned Phantom has surfaced on the black market with its original quantum-dot identifier still readable under deep UV — it traces back to a Tessera executive's personal armory.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, angular precision rifle with an exceptionally long suppressor assembly that dominates its silhouette. The weapon has a predatory, minimalist aesthetic—all hard lines and purposeful geometry. The integral suppressor creates the impression of a weapon designed to vanish acoustically before it vanishes visually.
physical_description.dimensions: Overall length: 118 cm | Barrel length: 61 cm (including 14-baffle suppressor) | Width at widest point: 8 cm | Height with low-profile optics mount: 12 cm
physical_description.weight_description: Balanced and controllable at 5.4 kg—heavy enough to absorb recoil smoothly, light enough for sustained precision work. The weight is distributed forward, giving it a purposeful heft rather than unwieldy bulk.
physical_description.primary_material: Aerospace-grade carbon composite with steel reinforcement at stress points. The thermal masking sleeve is a proprietary phase-change polymer composite.
physical_description.finish: Deep matte black with a barely-perceptible diamond-plate texture that resists reflection. The suppressor has a micro-brushed steel accents around baffle ports. Thermal sleeve shows a subtle iridescent oil-film patina from operational heating.
physical_description.color_scheme: Primary: Stealth matte black | Accents: brushed gunmetal gray on baffle ring, faint copper-tone heat discoloration on sleeve near muzzle
physical_description.grip_texture: Ergonomic polymer grip with aggressive crosshatch texturing, slightly tacky to resist slipping in gloved hands. The magazine well has raised ribbing for positive tactile feedback during reloads in low-light conditions.
distinctive_features: 14-baffle integral suppressor with visible serrated rings at baffle junctures
Thermal masking sleeve with microscopic heat-dispersal vanes running length of barrel
Quantum-dot serialization plate recessed into left receiver—faintly luminescent under certain angles
Minimal iron sights (co-witness height) with tritium inserts
Fluted receiver walls to reduce weight while maintaining structural integrity
Caseless ammunition magazine with transparent polymer sides showing round count
Integrated cable management channels routed along top rail for BCI optics tethering
Slight wear marks on stock shoulder—evidence of repeated deployment
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: TESSERA logo (angular Φ-derived geometric form) machined into upper receiver, left side. Quantum-dot identifier sits in recessed steel plate on left rail. Serial number acid-etched in faded numerals on lower receiver—deliberately worn-looking, possibly already 'cleaned' by a street armorist.
physical_description.condition_typical: Field-ready with light operational wear. The thermal sleeve shows faint heat stress marks. The suppressor baffles have minor carbon fouling visible in ports. Grip shows signs of gloved handling. Overall: meticulously maintained but used, never safe-queen pristine.
